# random_walks (Go rewrite)

## Generated by Claude

Go rewrite of the Python `make_random_walks` script. Queries the same DuckDB
database, builds its own in-memory graph (no igraph dependency), computes
random walks with a goroutine worker pool, and bulk-inserts results back into
`random_walks` via DuckDB's native Appender API.

## Why this should be faster

- **CSR adjacency graph** (two flat `[]int32` slices) instead of an igraph
  object — contiguous memory, no per-vertex object overhead, cache-friendly
  neighbor lookups.
- **Goroutines instead of OS processes.** No fork, no COW memory-duplication
  risk, no manual `chunksize` tuning — the `jobs` channel hands each worker
  one vertex at a time as it becomes free, so load balancing is automatic
  regardless of batch size.
- **Per-goroutine RNG** — no mutex contention generating random walk steps
  across cores.
- **DuckDB Appender** for bulk inserts — rows stream directly into DuckDB's
  columnar format instead of being parsed as SQL text or bound one row at a
  time.

## Build

Requires cgo (go-duckdb wraps the DuckDB C API) and network access the first
time, to fetch the dependency and generate `go.sum`:

```bash
go mod tidy
CGO_ENABLED=1 go build -o random_walks .
```

## Run

```bash
./random_walks \
  -db /path/to/your.duckdb \
  -workers 96 \
  -batch-size 9600 \
  -no-walks 100 \
  -max-walk-length 15
```

Flags:

| Flag               | Default            | Meaning                                             |
| ------------------ | ------------------ | --------------------------------------------------- |
| `-db`              | (required)         | Path to the DuckDB database file                    |
| `-no-walks`        | 100                | Random walks generated per vertex                   |
| `-max-walk-length` | 15                 | Max steps per walk                                  |
| `-batch-size`      | 9600               | Vertices per outer batch (progress logging / flush) |
| `-workers`         | `runtime.NumCPU()` | Number of concurrent walk-generating goroutines     |
| `-n-batches`       | 0 (= all)          | Stop after N batches, for quick testing             |

## Notes / things to verify on your machine

- **Undirected multigraph semantics preserved**: the original script built an
  `igraph.Graph()` (undirected by default) from `select distinct s, o from
triples` rows via `add_edges`. This rewrite mirrors that exactly — each row
  becomes a neighbor entry on _both_ endpoints, including duplicate parallel
  edges if the same `(s, o)` pair recurs. If you actually wanted a directed
  graph, or wanted parallel edges collapsed, that's a one-line change in the
  CSR-building loop (only add the `o -> s` direction, or dedupe edges first).
- **Walk termination on dead ends** mirrors igraph's behavior: if a vertex
  has no neighbors, the walk stops early and is shorter than
  `max-walk-length + 1` vertices.
- **Dedup** matches the Python `set()` of walk tuples — duplicate walks
  (by exact vertex sequence) for the same source vertex collapse to one.
- The `(s, o) -> excluding entities pointing at schema:dataFeedElement`
  filter discussed earlier isn't included here since it wasn't part of this
  request — it would slot into the edge-loading query/loop the same way it
  would in the Python version if you want it back.
- Double-check that `AppendRow(uint64, [][]uint64)` binds cleanly against
  your installed `go-duckdb/v2` version's `UBIGINT` / `UBIGINT[][]` handling
  — nested list appending is supported per the library's test suite, but
  driver versions do change; if you hit a binding error, pin the exact
  version in `go.mod` that you've verified works, or fall back to a
  `[][]uint64` → `[]interface{}` conversion if the driver wants `driver.Value`
  elements explicitly.
